title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
description: No-purchase activities at a free Flagstaff preserve, NAU’s public gallery, and Culture Pass destinations available to eligible NAU students.

cards.title: Walk Don Weaver Trail
cards.subtitle: Picture Canyon Natural & Cultural Preserve · Flagstaff
cards.notes: Bring water, follow the 0.7-mile route to views of the inner canyon, and leave the ruins and petroglyphs exactly as you find them.
cards.short_summary: A short preserve walk with canyon and riparian views.
cards.evidence_claim: The City lists Don Weaver as a 0.7-mile trail with inner-canyon, riparian, Pit House ruins, and Petroglyph Overlook views; the preserve is free and open year-round.
cards.access_notes: Free and open to the public year-round; the City notes some elevation change on this trail.

cards.title: Take the Tom Moody Loop
cards.subtitle: Picture Canyon Natural & Cultural Preserve · Flagstaff
cards.notes: Plan a relaxed 2.8-mile loop, stay on the route, and use the listed Water Bird petroglyph site as a viewing stop—not a touchpoint.
cards.short_summary: A relatively flat loop around the preserve.
cards.evidence_claim: The City describes Tom Moody Loop as a 2.8-mile, relatively flat route around the preserve that includes the Water Bird petroglyph site; preserve entry is free.
cards.access_notes: Free and open to the public year-round. Respect cultural-resource rules and do not climb on or mark petroglyphs.

cards.title: Pause at Petroglyph Overlook
cards.subtitle: Don Weaver Trail · Picture Canyon Natural & Cultural Preserve
cards.notes: Use the overlook to observe from a respectful distance, keep to the trail, and avoid touching, climbing on, or photographing artifacts up close.
cards.short_summary: A designated viewing point reached on Don Weaver Trail.
cards.evidence_claim: The City identifies Petroglyph Overlook as part of Don Weaver Trail and instructs visitors not to deface or remove cultural resources; the preserve is free.
cards.access_notes: Free and open to the public year-round; cultural-resource etiquette and laws apply.

cards.title: See the Water Bird Petroglyph Site
cards.subtitle: Tom Moody Loop · Picture Canyon Natural & Cultural Preserve
cards.notes: Follow Tom Moody Loop to the named site, look without handling the rock art, and let the visit be a low-impact shared history stop.
cards.short_summary: A named petroglyph viewing stop on the preserve loop.
cards.evidence_claim: The City says Tom Moody Loop includes the main Water Bird petroglyph site and prohibits defacing petroglyphs or removing artifacts; preserve access is free.
cards.access_notes: Free and open to the public year-round. Do not scratch on boulders, climb on them, or remove artifacts.

cards.title: Photograph Picture Canyon Waterfall
cards.subtitle: Picture Canyon Natural & Cultural Preserve · Flagstaff
cards.notes: Walk in with a camera or phone, frame the waterfall and ponderosa pine from allowed areas, and pack out anything you bring.
cards.short_summary: A year-round-water landmark in the city preserve.
cards.evidence_claim: The City identifies Flagstaff’s only waterfall at Picture Canyon and states that the preserve is free and open to the public year-round.
cards.access_notes: Free year-round public access; do not swim in the Rio de Flag or climb canyon walls.

cards.title: Walk the Arizona Trail Segment
cards.subtitle: Picture Canyon Natural & Cultural Preserve · Flagstaff
cards.notes: Use the easy-to-follow 1.5-mile segment for a walk-and-talk, then return on the marked trail while respecting preserve regulations.
cards.short_summary: A low-elevation-change section of the Arizona Trail.
cards.evidence_claim: The City lists a 1.5-mile Arizona Trail segment within Picture Canyon, says it has little elevation change, and states the preserve is free to the public.
cards.access_notes: Free and open to the public year-round; motorized vehicles are not allowed in the preserve.

cards.title: Browse Beasley Gallery
cards.subtitle: Performing and Fine Arts, Building 37, Room 216 · NAU
cards.notes: Drop in during Wednesday or Thursday public hours to view the rotating exhibitions, then check the gallery’s official channel for updates.
cards.short_summary: NAU’s public gallery for rotating and student exhibitions.
cards.evidence_claim: NAU states that Beasley Gallery is free and open to the public and gives current Wednesday–Thursday hours of 10 a.m.–4 p.m.
cards.access_notes: Free and open to the public; listed current hours are Wednesday and Thursday, 10 a.m.–4 p.m., or by appointment.

cards.title: Check Out a Lowell Culture Pass
cards.subtitle: Lowell Observatory · Flagstaff
cards.notes: Eligible NAU students can ask at Cline Library’s Ask Us! desk, confirm availability, and use the pass within its seven-day checkout window.
cards.short_summary: A free-admission option for two through Cline Library.
cards.evidence_claim: Cline Library lists Lowell Observatory among available Culture Pass venues; each pass provides one-time free general admission for two people.
cards.access_notes: Culture Pass checkouts are restricted to NAU/CCC students, faculty, and staff; availability is first-come, first-served and special events are excluded.

cards.title: Use a Culture Pass at MNA
cards.subtitle: Museum of Northern Arizona · Flagstaff
cards.notes: Check the pass inventory at Cline Library before making plans, then use the one-time general-admission benefit for a two-person museum outing.
cards.short_summary: Museum entry covered for two by an eligible Culture Pass.
cards.evidence_claim: Cline Library lists the Museum of Northern Arizona as an available Culture Pass venue and says each pass gives free general admission for two people.
cards.access_notes: For NAU/CCC students, faculty, and staff; passes are first-come, first-served and do not cover special events or separately ticketed activities.

cards.title: Reserve a Culture Pass for The Arb
cards.subtitle: The Arb at Flagstaff · Flagstaff
cards.notes: Start at Cline Library’s Ask Us! desk, verify a pass is available, and plan a two-person general-admission visit within seven days.
cards.short_summary: A Flagstaff garden visit covered by a library pass.
cards.evidence_claim: Cline Library lists The Arb at Flagstaff among available Culture Pass destinations and states that each pass is valid for free admission for two people.
cards.access_notes: Culture Pass access is for NAU/CCC students, faculty, and staff; passes are first-come, first-served and exclude special events.
